doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Growing up in the Bay Area
title: High school jazz combo during the war
summary: Only in senior year did he play, in a student combo at variety shows and veterans' hospitals in 1945.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But I didn’t play drums in high school because there was no orchestra. There was just a marching band for the football games and so forth. So I didn’t play anything in high school except maybe in my senior year some of the students organized a little jazz combo and they were searching frantically for a jazz pianist, so somehow they found me. So we
played for the variety shows that the high school had, and we went around the hospitals, the veterans’ hospitals and played — like this was 1945, so the war was still on.
Were you looking at military service down the road too?
